RP-02 execution progress: SLICE 1 (S1 mica-governing-buck) COMPLETE AND LANDED ON MAIN; S2 and S3 remain. Session log maxixe-ironic-kiskadee (d95a-aa80-dfe0-4336) holds the full trail and an exact resume point.

- 4758d47f82 / Gerrit 1880 — T1 vivacious-widish-indianabat: new binding_repository.py (360 LOC) as sole owner of live, retired, rotation and alert files.
- 1429cb8d4b / Gerrit 1885 — T2 evadable-curious-mastodon: facade delegation; binding_store.py 799 -> 710 LOC, now off the 800 cap.

HELD-OUT TDD EVIDENCE. T1: 27 tests authored RED-first against a signature-only scaffold (a bare ImportError was rejected as invalid RED); the implementer saw ONLY 12 happy-path tests, with 15 fault/corruption tests physically moved out of the worktree; all 27 then passed unseen. T2 was a refactor, so RED-first is the wrong gate — characterization tests are green before and after by design, and teeth were proven by 6 defect-seeded mutations instead. Refactoring litmus applied: a behavior-preserving rename of a private helper, attribute and constant left all tests green, so they are not change-detectors.

TWO FINDINGS THE HOLD-OUT AND MUTATION CAUGHT that no visible test would have:
1. T2 mutation found a genuine ORACLE GAP: replacing the facade's alias of the repository document with a shallow copy stayed GREEN across all 27 tests, because a shallow copy still shares the inner bindings/reverse dicts — only a NEW top-level key diverges. record_comment_id's setdefault('comment_ids') on a legacy store would therefore never reach the persisted bytes, silently losing comment identity and re-posting every mirrored comment (the DIG-5301 duplicate class). Closed with an 8th test.
2. T1 validation produced 2 held-out failures that were BOTH my test defects, each verified empirically rather than assumed: two monkeypatches collided because binding_repository.os and get_rotation.os are the same stdlib module, and a dedup test was over-specified against an aspirational docstring — a differential probe proved BindingStore emits 2 alerts too, so asserting 1 would have forced a behavior change this pure extraction was forbidden from making.

Both LLM-Review advisories on T2 were applied rather than deferred; both correctly flagged change-detector coupling in my own tests (rendered-annotation assertions, and an exact ordered call trace). One Verified -1 was root-caused to a stale generated file (docs/env-vars.md line reference shifted by the refactor) and fixed; a second was traced to a KNOWN tracked macOS flake (tapestried-abhorrent-tuna closed, asbestos-popular-tench in_progress) and recheck'd with that reasoning stated per CONTRIBUTING.md section 6 — never a blind retry. That flake is now fixed on main by 9f7407bb3d.

NEXT: S2 brainy-cooked-hog is now unblocked but UNSIGNED — run review-plan on it (only valid now that S1 is closed), then claim, then its three tasks in order 6083 -> f59b -> 2419. The session log records eight verified constraints for the remaining work, the most load-bearing being that S2 MUST re-register both moved config reads in scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py in the same change or the pre-commit hook blocks the commit outright.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RP-02 progress: SLICES 1 AND 2 COMPLETE AND LANDED ON MAIN (6 of 9 tasks, 2 of 3 stories). S3 convergent-pinelike-lunamoth remains and is now unblocked. Full trail and an exact resume point are in session log maxixe-ironic-kiskadee (d95a-aa80-dfe0-4336).

LANDED, each with LLM-Review +1 AND Verified +1, submitted individually per the AGENTS.md no-feature-branch fallback: 4758d47f82 (S1T1 repository) / 1429cb8d4b (S1T2 facade delegation) / 0c318685c8 (S1T3 ADR 0099 + publication guards) / 9371328844 (S2T1 identity transitions) / 250cac4d8c (S2T2 absence, tombstone, comment) / 9c3db3ea12 (S2T3 narrow rich-emission seam).

OUTCOME SO FAR: binding_store.py 799 -> 561 LOC, off the cap it was pinned against. Three internal owners exist behind one unchanged public facade: binding_repository.py 360, binding_lifecycle.py 533. ADR 0099 records the design. ~130 new tests.

THE EPIC'S MOST TRANSFERABLE FINDING: four DOCUMENTED behaviours turned out never to have been implemented, each caught by writing the test the docstring implied and watching it fail against faithful code. (1) 'safety-abort on ambiguous double bind' - bind_confirm is last-writer-wins with no abort anywhere in the three modules; this one was asserted by S2's plan AND its parent story AC, so both were corrected and the term reserved for S3, where the abort is genuinely new. (2) Lifecycle alerts are documented as deduped, but is_deduped compares a timestamp_ns that no caller stamps, so suppression can never fire. (3) The comment map's 'a key is never remapped to a different id' - the change-gate is equality-only, so a differing id overwrites. (4) The rich-emission op was credited with save/dirty-gating behaviour, but the production caller never saves per emit and save() is explicitly unconditional. In every case I pinned the REAL behaviour and corrected the false statement rather than changing behaviour inside an extraction slice, and filed the ones that are genuine defects.

MUTATION ALSO CLOSED THREE ORACLE GAPS my tests would otherwise have shipped: a facade copying the repository document (invisible until a NEW top-level key diverges, which would have silently lost comment identity and re-posted every mirrored comment); a rebind fixture that could not distinguish a targeted reverse pop from a sweep; and a save spy watching only the facade while the policy owner holds the repository directly.

HELD-OUT TDD held throughout: implementers saw only happy-path subsets, and every withheld discriminator passed unseen (15/15, 4/4, 11/11, 13/13, 5/5 across the five code slices). Every CI failure was root-caused, never retried - a stale generated env-vars doc twice, a comment-hygiene gate rejecting a commit SHA in a source comment, and one known tracked macOS flake recheck'd with reasoning per CONTRIBUTING.md section 6.

NEXT: S3 is the only slice with genuinely NEW behaviour (interrupted-retirement completion), so RED-first applies properly rather than characterization. Its three tasks run c4f7 -> 90a5 -> ef69. All are UNSIGNED; set file_impact before earning each attestation. Eight verified constraints are recorded in the session log, the sharpest being that run_differs.py has only 61 lines of headroom so S3 T2's edit there is the invocation only, and that S2 T3 has now made the apply_handlers docstring claim about 'cannot carry a narrower accessor' false, so S3 T3 must update it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
ORDERING CORRECTION for S3, recorded here as a comment because the epic's description is signed and a text edit would stale its attestation.

The epic's architectural-constraint list says live recovery runs "after configuration snapshot/preflight and exclusive lock/staleness validation but before remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation." Two parts of that turned out not to hold against the actual spine, and S3's story plan and file impact have been corrected accordingly (S3 was unsigned at the time, so the correction was made before earning its attestation, and the corrected plan then passed review-plan with 0 blocking).

What was verified by reading reconcile.py:
1. `_load_snapshots(ctx)` is called at reconcile.py:222 and internally constructs the binding store (:280), runs the under-lock staleness gate (:281-282), creates the first write-bearing artifact (:286), and performs the FIRST remote issue fetch (:328-333).
2. `bind_operation_runtime` — the immutable operation/config snapshot — is composed at :227, i.e. AFTER `_load_snapshots` returns and therefore AFTER that fetch. So "after the configuration snapshot AND before the remote fetch" is an EMPTY window in the current code.
3. `run_differs()` is invoked at :231, also after the fetch, and the existing `recover_pending_bindings` call inside it (run_differs.py:418) therefore already runs post-fetch. No point inside run_differs.py can precede remote observation.

Resolution: the pre-observation requirement is the load-bearing half, because its stated purpose is to stop an upgraded pass interleaving new liveness evidence with completion. Retirement completion reads only local binding state and has no dependency on the operation config snapshot, so the snapshot conjunct was dropped rather than satisfied; where that snapshot is composed remains RP-04's decision. The invocation therefore lands in reconcile.py immediately after the staleness gate, and run_differs.py needs no edit at all.

Consequence worth flagging for anyone planning further work here: the binding constraint is NOT run_differs.py's 61 lines of headroom, it is reconcile.py's SIX (794 of the 800 cap). So the spine gets a single call line and every guard lives in binding_recovery.py. reconcile.py is also in RP-04 S7.3.a's impact set, so that file is contested.

SEPARATE FINDING, filed as easygoing-tremendous-frogmouth (7851-e06b-9e85-4c9e) discovered_from the S3 story: the existing create-recovery call has NO write-bearing gate, only `if not scoped_ids`, and is handed the real configured transport. So a `preview` or `--mode dry-run` pass performs remote `add_label` / `set_entity_property` writes while `persist=False` suppresses the local save that would have recorded them. The invariant-filing gate immediately beside it composes both axes (`(not persist) or bool(scoped_ids)`), so the omission is asymmetric with its own neighbour. S3 pins this behaviour rather than changing it — S3 T1 carries an explicit AC that the create-recovery gate is unchanged — because it is a behaviour change to anti-duplicate machinery and needs its own plan.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
=== RESIDUAL-GAP DISPOSITION SWEEP (pre-epic-close) ===

Completed by the coordinating session after the S3 executor agent died on a stall watchdog mid-audit, immediately after T3 landed. Every enumerable gap this run produced gets exactly one disposition below.

FILED (6 tickets, all linked):
1. smalltime-rapid-elk (2e1f) discovered_from S1 T1 — lifecycle alerts can never dedupe: is_deduped compares a timestamp_ns no caller stamps. Currently in_progress.
2. best-kingly-monkey discovered_from S2, relates_to RP-04 S7.3.a — retarget RP-04's config reads to binding_lifecycle.py. NOW CLOSED: RP-04 acted on it, and its C3f commit message states outright 'This does NOT reach whole-tree EMPTY: the two binding_lifecycle.py rows remain (RP-04 S7.3.a's retarget)'. The soft relates_to plus a filed ticket was sufficient; no cross-root blocking link was needed.
3. captious-hennish-mangabey discovered_from S2 T3 — integration idempotency oracle patches binding_store_mod._now_iso but clear_absent now resolves it from binding_lifecycle, so the patch no longer reaches it. In_progress.
4. easygoing-tremendous-frogmouth discovered_from S3 — preview and dry-run passes perform remote add_label/set_entity_property writes during create recovery: the call's only guard is 'if not scoped_ids' and it receives the real configured transport, while the invariant-filing gate beside it composes both axes. S3 deliberately pinned that gate UNCHANGED rather than widening scope to fix it. In_progress.
5. insectile-modest-martin discovered_from S3, relates_to both RP-03 S5 tickets — preserve the pre-observation repair boundary when reconcile.py is extracted. Open.
6. frangible-irongray-adouri discovered_from this epic — the packaged rebar release omits _engine_support/commit_impact.py, so close_precheck._check_file_impact_vs_diff raises ImportError on ANY close with recorded file_impact when running an installed build, AND the process still exits 0, so an automated caller records a close that never happened. Hit while closing S3; worked around by closing from a worktree on the checkout's venv build.

FIXED IN SCOPE (false documented claims corrected rather than implemented — nine total across the epic; implementing them would have injected unrequested behaviour change into pure extractions):
- 'safety-abort on ambiguous double bind' — bind_confirm is last-writer-wins with no abort anywhere. S2's plan AND its parent story AC both asserted it; both corrected, and the term reserved for S3 where the abort is genuinely new.
- comment map 'never remapped' — the gate is equality-only, so a differing id overwrites. Docstring corrected; a byte-comparison test that could not fail was replaced with a write-counting oracle and re-verified RED under mutation.
- rich-emission per-emit save/dirty-gating — the caller never saves per emit and save() is unconditional. AC corrected to 'performs NO save of its own on ANY path'.
- apply_handlers' justification that binding_store.py 'sits at the module-size cap and cannot carry a narrower accessor' — false once S2 T3 added note_rich_emit; rewritten in T3.
- binding_lifecycle's claim that recovery 'stays with BindingStore' — corrected.
- the dc-live-oracle label-writer census, which greps SOURCE TEXT keyed on FILE NAME and named binding_store.py as the third colon-form writer — retargeted to binding_recovery.py after verifying exactly three production writers remain.
- this epic's own architectural-constraint list, whose 'after configuration snapshot AND before remote fetch' conjunction describes an EMPTY window: _load_snapshots constructs the store, runs the staleness gate and performs the FIRST remote fetch in one call, while bind_operation_runtime composes afterwards. Recorded as a comment rather than a description edit, deliberately, so the epic's signed attestation did not go stale. The pre-observation half was kept because it is load-bearing; the snapshot conjunct was dropped because completion reads only local binding state.

ACCEPTED (no action, with reason):
- _env_int's minimum clamp is behaviourally UNOBSERVABLE through note_absent, because the counter increments before the comparison, so grace 0 or -3 retires on the first 404 exactly as a clamped 1 does. No test was manufactured for an unobservable difference — that would assert internal structure. Moot now regardless: RP-04 C3g cut that read to config.resolve_absent_retire_grace and deleted _env_int.
- reconcile.py finishing at 799/800, one line of headroom. Accepted rather than pre-emptively extracted: the extraction belongs to whoever needs the space (RP-03 S5), and insectile-modest-martin guards the ordering constraint through it. Extracting speculatively here would have exceeded S3's scope.
- Held-out artifacts under /tmp/rp02-heldout/ were not preserved durably. Accepted: every discriminator is now committed in the landed test suites, so the scratch copies have no remaining value.

PROCESS LESSONS worth carrying (recorded in session log maxixe-ironic-kiskadee): 'make lint' does NOT cover every Verified gate — check_comment_hygiene.py, make config-check, check_verify_gate_parity.py, check_dco_identity.py, check_criteria_vocabulary.py, check_skill_frontmatter.py, zizmor and actionlint all run as separate CI steps; and a subsystem-scoped regression run misses repo-wide guards living outside the subsystem tree. Also: no source comment in this repo may cite a commit SHA — cite the TICKET — which matters for an epic whose whole method is characterising pre-extraction behaviour.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SWEEP ADDENDUM — a seventh gap ticket, and the epic-close policy decision.

7. seraphic-taming-terrier (3ed6-b264-e1ae-41a0) discovered_from this epic, relates_to frangible-irongray-adouri — rebar's LLM gate operations (close with the completion gate, review-plan, verify-completion) emit NO output between start and verdict, so a supervisor treating silence as no-progress kills a healthy run. This is the root cause of the S3 executor agent's death: it was killed by a 600s stall watchdog at the epic-close step with all nine of its changes already landed, stranding the epic and one story in_progress with every descendant closed. Independently reproduced twice in the completing session: the S3 close blew a 600s foreground timeout and emitted only unrelated enrich_drain warnings before its final line, and review-plan on this epic did the same.

The two tooling bugs COMPOUND, which is why they are cross-linked: seraphic-taming-terrier makes a SUCCESSFUL close look hung, while frangible-irongray-adouri makes a CRASHED close look successful (ImportError, then exit 0). A supervisor that survives the silence may then be told exit 0 by a close that never happened. Anyone automating rebar closes should read them together.

EPIC-CLOSE POLICY, decided by the operator: the epic closes now with all seven gaps FILED, LINKED and dispositioned rather than fixed. Rationale recorded for the next reader: the gaps are discovered_from links, not children, so rebar's structural open-children guard does not block this close — the requirement was a judgment call, not a tool constraint. Three of the seven are already in_progress. One, insectile-modest-martin, is deliberately NOT closeable: it exists to constrain the reconcile.py extraction RP-03 S5 has not yet performed, so closing it would destroy its only purpose. The three RP-02-discovered defects (alert dedup, the stale idempotency patch target, and remote Jira writes during preview/dry-run create recovery) are LATENT and PRE-EXISTING — this epic surfaced them by characterising documented behaviour, it did not introduce them, and fixing them inside a pure-extraction epic was explicitly out of scope.

CLOSE MECHANICS worth recording, since both gates fired legitimately on this close: the first attempt was refused with 'plan-review close gate: stale-pin-drift — reviewed related-ticket material is stale ... targets: 486a-69ef-6370-48ff child stale-pin-drift, fc1c-1b08-70c2-4afb child stale-pin-drift'. That was CORRECT: this epic's attestation pins its children's material, and both S2 and S3 had their plans legitimately corrected during execution (S2's phantom double-bind safety-abort; S3's run_differs.py-to-reconcile.py ordering error). Remediated by re-running review-plan on the epic, which returned certified — not by --force. The close also had to run from a git worktree at 0b851c8103 using the checkout's venv build, because the shared main checkout must never be fast-forwarded to satisfy a close and the global packaged build is broken per gap 6.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`BindingStore` is the authoritative local-id ↔ Jira identity aggregate and must remain so, but its 799-line module now owns byte persistence, live/reverse lifecycle policy, retirement, recovery, peer-state delegates, comment identity, and GET rotation. New safety rules have no cohesive owner, and production code mutates an inner entry returned by the shallow `all_bindings()` compatibility query. A mechanical split could regress hard-won crash, index-lag, identity, serialization, and selective-publication behavior.

## Outcome
Keep one public `BindingStore` facade and existing import/method compatibility while extracting three internal owners: a byte-preserving repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, and incomplete-operation recovery. Typed views remain open over the original dictionaries so unknown fields and exact JSON behavior survive. Add the approved journal-free retirement completion rule: a durable tombstone is authoritative intent, and a live forward/reverse pair is removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree. Only explicit `unretire` revokes that intent; automatic liveness observations never resurrect a tombstoned identity.

## Delivery slices
1. Extract repository/unit-of-work persistence behind the facade with byte, fault-cut, corruption, rotation-order, and selective-publication regression oracles; establish ADR 0099 with the complete approved target design.
2. Extract lifecycle policy and add narrow facade operations so new production code no longer needs mutation-through-query while `all_bindings()` remains shallow-compatible.
3. Extract recovery, cut the live caller to the narrow mutation seam, complete exact-match interrupted retirements before remote issue observation, and finalize ADR 0099 to describe the realized behavior.

## Architectural constraints
- Preserve `peer_state.py`, `get_rotation.py`, pending → confirmed → reversible retired lifecycle, numeric-ID re-key, comment identity, and the existing five-file selective tickets publication.
- Preserve unknown fields, `indent=2`, sorted keys, trailing newline, legacy additive reads, and unchanged-pass byte/HEAD idempotency.
- Corrupt live state still fails closed; retired/rotation/alert/commit failure behavior changes only when this plan names it.
- Construction, load, check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered operations do not perform recovery writes.
- Live recovery runs after configuration snapshot/preflight and exclusive lock/staleness validation but before remote issue fetch, binding walk, differ, or lifecycle mutation. This ordering prevents an upgraded pass from interleaving new liveness evidence with completion.
- In a historical overlap, stale `absent_404_count`, automatic 200/`clear_absent`, or same-key confirm cannot revoke the durable tombstone; only explicit `unretire` removes it and thereby eliminates the completion candidate.
- No general journal, format migration, eager rewrite, broad `git add -A`, deep-copy change to `all_bindings()`, or new identity writer.

## Compatibility / rollback
Each slice is an internal facade delegation with unchanged stored formats and public signatures. A slice can be reverted independently to the preceding facade implementation. The exact-match repair is additive and idempotent: disabling its pre-observation live-operation call restores the prior detectable overlap without rewriting coherent stores. Rollback never deletes a remote issue or implies automatic unretire.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Existing `BindingStore` imports, signatures, shallow `all_bindings()` behavior, unknown-field preservation, and exact serialization remain compatible through direct-loader and public-facade tests.
- [x] Repository fault-cut tests preserve current rotation-before-live ordering, per-file atomic replacement, selective five-file publication, and explicit failure outcomes.
- [x] Lifecycle tests preserve both-index identity guards, pending/confirmed/retired rules, 404 grace/reset, immutable-ID re-key, tombstone suppression/unretire, and append-only comment identity.
- [x] Recovery tests prove keyed/keyless create recovery and exact-match retirement completion are idempotent; repair runs before remote observation, identities must agree, and ambiguity/replace failure safety-aborts.
- [x] Automatic liveness signals do not override durable retirement intent; explicit `unretire` removes the tombstone and prevents completion.
- [x] Load/check/dry-run/preview/selection/filtered tests prove zero recovery writes; only a validated write-bearing operation may repair an interrupted retirement.
- [x] ADR 0099 identifies preserved behavior, the intentional repair behavior, explicit-unretire reversal, pre-observation ordering, rollback, and the prohibition on broad tickets-branch staging.

file_impact.reason: Stable public facade over the new internal owners.
